guide: Turn an AI coding assistant into a pre-launch compliance checklist for your app, so legal and privacy groundwork is done before you release. You need an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT or Codex), a web version of your app, and a place to host the pages.
1. Open Claude and ask it to produce a pre-launch checklist as an artifact, covering what your app type needs before release.
1. Make sure the list includes legal review, a privacy policy, terms of service, a cookie policy and a support or contact page.
1. Ask the assistant to mark each item as done, missing or needs a lawyer, based on what your app actually does with user data.
1. Have Claude Code or Codex build the missing pages (privacy, terms, cookies, support) in your web app and link them from the footer or sidebar.
1. Deploy the updated site to a host such as Vercel so the pages have public URLs.
1. Add a demo account so reviewers and early users can look around without signing up.
1. Re-run the checklist before each release, including the Android and iOS store submissions, and tick items off as you finish them.
Watch out: an AI-written checklist and policy pages are a starting point, not legal advice, so have a qualified person review anything that carries legal weight.

```
You are helping me prepare my app for public launch. The app is <app name>, a <one-line description>. It runs as a <web app / mobile app> built with <tech stack>, hosted on <host>. It collects <types of user data, e.g. email, location, photos> and I plan to release on <web / Android / iOS> in <country or region>.
First, produce a pre-launch compliance checklist as a single document I can tick through. Cover at least: legal review, privacy policy, terms of service, cookie policy, a support or contact page, data deletion and account removal, and app store requirements for <stores>. Mark each item as done, missing or needs a professional, based on what the app does.
Then, for every missing page, write a first draft in plain English and add it to my codebase as a route linked from the footer. Do not invent company details; use placeholders like <company name> and <contact email>.
Return the checklist, the list of files you changed, and a short note on which items I should have a lawyer review.
```
